Core purpose

Pick up, deliver and hand over letters, documents, parcels and similar items within or between institutions, complete delivery and collection along routes and to time requirements, and ensure items arrive on time, signatures are clear and pickup and delivery are traceable.

Core purpose of adjacent positions: light truck drivers drive light trucks to transport goods and load and unload; cargo and freight agents arrange cargo transport and handle documents; shipping, receiving and inventory clerks handle receiving and dispatch and inventory registration; dispatchers arrange staff, vehicles and routes; mail clerks sort and process mail; and postal mail carriers deliver mail along postal delivery routes.
Main objects and basis
Items to be delivered and collected, delivery information and recipients, and dispatch and routes; the basis is the unit's delivery and safety procedures and its timeliness and route requirements.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: goods and freight documents (light truck drivers), freight contracts and transport arrangements (freight agents), receiving and dispatch and inventory documents (shipping and receiving clerks), vehicles, staff and routes (dispatchers), mail and sorting rules (mail clerks), and mail and delivery routes (postal carriers).
Core process
Collect and check → plan the route → load and depart → pick up and deliver → record signatures → unload, sort and confirm.

Processes of adjacent positions: loading, transport and delivery (light truck drivers), arranging transport and handling documents (freight agents), receiving and dispatch registration and stocktaking (shipping and receiving clerks), rostering, dispatch and scheduling (dispatchers), sorting, processing and distribution (mail clerks), and delivery along routes (postal mail carriers).
Main outputs
On-time pickup and delivery, clear signature and payment collection records, and complete pickup, delivery and exception ledgers.

Responsible party

Couriers and messengers are responsible for checking items, delivering on time, the accuracy of signatures and payments collected on behalf of others, and the traceability of pickup, delivery and exception records; major changes to routes and time requirements, compensation beyond authority and hazardous goods handling are not decided by them alone.

Responsible parties of adjacent positions: light truck drivers are responsible for driving and cargo safety; freight agents for transport arrangements and documents; shipping and receiving clerks for receiving, dispatch and inventory accuracy; dispatchers for dispatch and route arrangements; mail clerks for sorting and processing; and postal carriers for delivery along routes.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate by process with team colleagues, dispatch, branches and customer service; when facing delivery exceptions, damaged items, recipient disputes, road and safety risks or matters beyond authorization, escalate according to procedures and keep records; demonstrate according to the process when training new colleagues.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: light truck drivers work with the warehouse and dispatch; freight agents with carriers and customers; shipping and receiving clerks with the warehouse and purchasing; dispatchers with drivers and branches; mail clerks with the sorting center; and postal carriers with branches and sorting.

Drive light trucks to transport goods and load and unload, completing multi-stop delivery along a route.

Arrange cargo transport and handle freight documents, quotations and customer liaison.

The difference is that the object is freight contracts and transport arrangements, usually handled indoors as documents rather than on-route pickup and delivery; the O*NET national median annual wage is 52,260 USD.

Dispatchers, Except Police, Fire, and Ambulance (43-5032.00, adjacent occupation)

The difference is that the object is arranging staff and vehicles, and the output is dispatch and scheduling records, without directly delivering on route; the O*NET national median annual wage is 50,340 USD.

Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators (43-9051.00, adjacent occupation)
The difference is that the work is indoor sorting and processing of mail, usually without on-route delivery and signature collection; the O*NET national median annual wage is 39,280 USD.

values: Fictional pickup and delivery scenario materials (exercise inputs)

Fictional scenario: a delivery worker at a fictional same-city distribution station faces three problems in one day. The first recipient asks for a last-minute change of address to ② kilometers away, but the new address is not on the original route; the second recipient is not at home and the telephone is unanswered, so the parcel needs an alternative delivery arrangement or return; the third parcel has a damaged outer box with signs of leakage, and the recipient asks to refuse it and claim compensation. In that day's dispatch sheet, one payment collection entry only says 'received', with no amount and no handler; and one vehicle's departure check sheet does not record tyre pressure.

Materials provided: the dispatch and route sheet; recipient information and delivery instructions; a delivery and signature record template; a summary of the address change and refusal policy; the compensation and reporting process; and the departure check sheet and vehicle information.

Materials not provided: the authority to adjust the route for a last-minute address change, the compensation approval authority for the damaged parcel, and the specific rules for choosing between an alternative delivery arrangement and return when the recipient is absent. If the exercise requires these conditions, please clearly write down your assumptions and the parties you need to confirm with.
Task requirements

Please write a one-page pickup and delivery handling and handover plan: including the handling order for the last-minute address change, checking and the alternative delivery or return arrangement when the recipient is absent, evidence preservation and reporting for the damaged parcel, how to correct the missing payment collection entry, and how to handle the missing departure check item and the handover items.

The plan should state which information comes from the scenario materials and which is still assumptions, and explain whether it relies on the dispatch sheet, the record template or the policy summary.
Reference deliverable (derivable from the scenario)

The plan should include: the address change (first verify the new address and route feasibility; if it can be adjusted, adjust according to procedures and notify dispatch; if not, explain and ask, without going off route on your own), the absent recipient (check the conditions for alternative delivery or return according to policy, keep the call and visit records, and do not leave the item or sign on the recipient's behalf without authorization), the damaged parcel (take photographs as evidence, isolate the leaking item, handle it according to the reporting process, and if beyond your authority submit for approval without paying compensation first), payments (make an explanatory correction to the 'received' record, stating the amount, handler and time, without altering the original record), the departure check (back-fill the tyre pressure and note the source and that it is to be verified; if it cannot be confirmed, record it as to be verified and hand it over) and handover (clearly state the status of the three transactions, the actions taken and the items still to be confirmed).
The reference deliverable only lists the elements that should be included and does not require the exact wording of the example; being able to explain the basis for the judgment is enough.
Boundaries and conclusions that cannot be inferred

This exercise only tests pickup and delivery checking, route and exception handling, evidence preservation and escalation awareness; it does not evaluate whether a real unit's handling is compliant and does not constitute a hiring, authorization or real compensation handling recommendation.
Do not use real unit, customer or payment information; any real payments, compensation and data permissions must be handled according to your unit's rules.

entries.answer: Receive the items to be delivered and the delivery information (recipient name, address, telephone and delivery instructions), sort by route and plan the most time-saving route, load the vehicle by list and pay attention to hazardous goods, walk, ride, drive or take public transport to deliver and collect letters, documents, parcels and similar items at the destination, record the items collected and delivered and the recipient's response, obtain signatures or cash-on-collection payments, unload and sort, transfer cargo from larger vehicles to small vehicles, open and sort incoming items, and complete routine vehicle maintenance and general receiving, dispatch and clerical affairs.
entries.question: What does the daily work of couriers and messengers involve?

entries.answer: Couriers and messengers pick up, deliver and hand over items within or between institutions and carry responsibility for item count checking, signatures and cash-on-collection payments; light truck drivers mainly drive trucks to transport whole loads and load and unload; dispatchers arrange staff, vehicles and routes and issue dispatch orders without delivering on route themselves; cargo and freight agents handle freight documents and transport arrangements; shipping, receiving and inventory clerks handle receiving, dispatch and inventory registration; and mail clerks sort and process mail indoors.
entries.question: How do couriers and messengers differ from light truck drivers and dispatchers?

entries.answer: Route planning and navigation, dispatch and electronic waybills, delivery status returns and automatic notifications, and recipient self-service sending and collection and smart lockers can reduce manual planning, registration and part of the handover; but on-route pickup and delivery, face-to-face delivery and signatures, on-site judgment under road and weather conditions, item inspection and hazardous goods handling, and exception and compensation handling still depend on people and are constrained by unit procedures and safety requirements. Technical exposure is not equal to organizational adoption or job disappearance.
entries.question: How will AI affect or replace couriers and messengers?

entries.answer: What can be verified is change at the task level: the three task categories of route planning and dispatch, delivery status and notification, and end-point sending and collection and smart lockers can be partly taken on by tools; this page has no single-occupation adoption rate or displacement data.

entries.answer: Delivery information checking, route and timeliness arrangements, loading and hazardous goods handling, the accuracy of signatures and cash-on-collection payments, item status inspection and exception documentation, and review and privacy awareness when using systems.

description.text: Couriers and messengers (O*NET-SOC 43-5021.00) pick up, deliver and hand over letters, documents, parcels and other items within or between institutions: this covers collecting items and delivery information, planning routes, loading and pickup and delivery, recording collection and delivery, unloading and sorting, obtaining signatures and cash-on-collection payments, routine vehicle maintenance and receiving and dispatch and clerical affairs; it includes the U.S. 2025 median annual wage of 39,200 USD (hourly wage 18.85 USD), about 247,200 people employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 employment projection much faster than average (7% or higher), the mainland China occupation-level wage and employment basis gap, and the control points for road and weather exposure, time pressure and item safety responsibility.

subject.name: Couriers and messengers
subject.summary: Couriers and messengers correspond in the United States to O*NET-SOC 43-5021.00 (Couriers and Messengers). The core is picking up, delivering and handing over letters, documents, parcels and other items within or between institutions: collecting items and delivery information by dispatch or route, planning and following the most time-saving route, loading the vehicle and paying attention to hazardous goods, picking up and delivering en route, recording collection and delivery information, unloading and sorting by route, obtaining signatures and cash-on-collection payments, completing routine vehicle maintenance and attendance confirmation, and taking on receiving and dispatch and general clerical affairs when needed. On the China side, similar positions are mostly called couriers, same-city delivery riders, parcel deliverers, or internal couriers and receiving and dispatch clerks and are not a one-to-one correspondence with this U.S. detailed occupation, so appointment and pay bases cannot be interchanged.
